sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
essence: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions.
story: During the epic Mahabharata war, the great warrior Arjuna was paralyzed by doubt, refusing to fight his own relatives. Lord Krishna delivered this powerful Shloka to teach him 'Karma Yoga' (the path of detached action). Krishna explained that focusing on the result creates anxiety, while focusing purely on performing one's duty brings supreme peace.

sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही॥
essence: Just as a person discards old clothes and puts on new ones, the soul discards old bodies and enters new ones.
story: To cure Arjuna of his deep grief over the potential death of his loved ones, Lord Krishna revealed the immortal nature of the soul. He used the simple, everyday analogy of changing clothes to demonstrate that death is not the end, but merely a transition of the eternal soul into a new physical vessel.

sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
essence: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice and a predominant rise of irreligion, at that time I descend Myself.
story: Krishna makes a profound promise to humanity in this verse. He declares that the Divine will always intervene when evil outweighs good. This gave Arjuna the courage to fight, knowing that by fighting the righteous war, he was acting as an instrument of the Divine will to restore cosmic balance.

sanskrit:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥
essence: One must elevate himself by his own mind, not degrade himself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.
story: Here, Krishna introduces the concept of self-mastery. He explains to Arjuna that no external force can truly defeat or elevate a person; it all depends on one's own mind. A disciplined mind acts as one's greatest friend, while an uncontrolled mind acts as the worst enemy.

sanskrit:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः॥
essence: If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it.
story: Krishna simplifies the concept of worship, emphasizing that true devotion does not require wealth or elaborate rituals. It is the purity of the intention and the love in the heart that matters most. This taught Arjuna that spiritual perfection is accessible to everyone, regardless of their material status.
